Note there is no `timestamp_unit` knob anywhere in this lane. The recipe
book declares `timestamp[us]` and the engine produces datetime64[us]
directly, so unlike the pandas-mediated database lanes there is no ns->us
cast to configure — one fewer place a lossy conversion could hide.
_discriminators_comment: RF-002 legitimately does not apply to this dataset. The 90-day Berlin
archive window contains 2160 hourly readings and ZERO nulls — checked at
the source, not assumed — so there is no column that can discriminate
This is exactly the case the declaration rule exists to distinguish: an
empty `discriminators` list WITH a stated reason yields SKIPPED-with-reason,
while omitting the key entirely is a FAIL. 'There is nothing nullable here'
and 'nobody thought about it' must never produce the same verdict.
If a future window includes a gap (the reanalysis does occasionally have
them), declare temperature_2m here with its exact count and the check
upgrades itself from SKIPPED to a real gate.
discriminators_absent_reason: the open-meteo archive window 2026-01-01..2026-03-31 for Berlin returns 2160 hourly readings with zero nulls in temperature_2m (verified at the source), so no column can discriminate count(col) from count(*)
_boundary_comment: B-2 applies to APIs exactly as it does to databases. A provider that
silently answered in local time instead of UTC would shift every timestamp
uniformly, and count, null count and both scaled sums would all still
match. min/max is the only declared check here that moves.
The probe records the provider's own declared timezone (`GMT`) alongside
the bounds, because agreeing bounds mean something different when the
provider says GMT than when it says something else.

aggregates._note: AUTHORITY. Temperatures carry one decimal, so round(t*10) is exact per value and integer addition is associative.
Corroborates only. Summing float64 first is order-sensitive.
